title: Create board updates from your operating data
description: A system that turns your raw metrics and notes into a draft board update organized around performance, progress, risks, and what you need from the board.

diff.title: Diff
diff.content: A side-by-side view of what changed between two versions of a file. Red lines were removed, green lines were added. When Claude shows you a diff, it's previewing exactly what's about to change before you approve.

agent.title: Agent
agent.content: An AI that works independently to complete a goal — planning steps, picking tools, running them, and deciding what to do next without you prompting it at every step. Unlike a chatbot, an agent takes action.

model.title: Model
model.content: A specific trained version of an AI. Claude has several models (like Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) that differ in capability and speed. Larger models are smarter but slower; smaller ones are faster and cheaper.

skill.title: Skill
skill.content: A plain-text file with instructions for a specific repeatable workflow. Save it once, then trigger it with a slash command like /research-competitive. Same steps and output format every time — like a macro for Claude.

stack.title: Stack
stack.content: The set of tools something is built with or that you work with. An app's stack is its languages and services, from database to frontend (the Leland Courses stack is Astro, Tailwind, Cloudflare, and Supabase). Your AI stack is the toolkit you've assembled for your own work — chat tools, agents, automations, and the connectors that tie them together.

claude.title: Claude
claude.content: The AI made by Anthropic. Available as a chat tool at claude.ai, as a desktop app (Claude Desktop), and as a terminal tool (Claude Code). The different interfaces are suited for different types of work.

notion.title: Notion
notion.content: An all-in-one workspace for docs, wikis, databases, and project tracking. Used heavily across the AI Builder program as a destination for AI-generated content and as a connected app in Level 2 automations.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.content: The instruction or message you give to an AI. The quality of your prompt directly shapes the quality of the output. Writing better prompts is one of the highest-leverage skills in this program.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.content: The written definition of what a good output looks like, in 3–5 scoreable dimensions. Evals grade against a rubric; without one, 'is this good?' is a vibe, not a measurement.

chatgpt.title: ChatGPT
chatgpt.content: OpenAI's chat assistant. The most widely known AI tool — works similarly to Claude but with different strengths and weaknesses. Useful to have access to for cross-checking outputs or trying alternate models.

context.title: Context
context.content: Everything Claude can 'see' in a given session — your messages, files you've shared, instructions, and conversation history. The more relevant context you give Claude, the better its output.

tool-connectors.title: Tool Connectors
tool-connectors.content: Integrations that let Claude read from and write to apps you use (Gmail, Slack, Google Calendar, Notion, HubSpot, etc.). Set up once in Customize → Connectors. Each connector opens up a new category of tasks Claude can automate.

personal-knowledge-base.title: Personal Knowledge Base
personal-knowledge-base.content: A store of your own accumulated knowledge — notes, decisions, references — organized so an AI can search and use it. The difference from a pile of documents: structure and maintenance. Level 2 builds one as a wiki.

children.text: 97% of executives say they personally benefit from AI, but only 29% see meaningful organizational ROI, per [WRITER's research on enterprise AI adoption](https://writer.com/blog/enterprise-ai-adoption-2026/). A board update is where that gap shows up directly. It's the moment individual wins either roll up into one org-level story or stay scattered across a dozen private wins.

60% of executives already use AI regularly to support their own decisions, per [Deloitte's 2026 Global Human Capital Trends report](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/topics/talent/human-capital-trends/2026/decision-making-with-ai.html), which means board audiences increasingly expect the reasoning behind a number alongside the number itself. This system turns that raw data into a draft update covering performance, progress, risks, and what you're asking the board for.

Run it as a monthly or quarterly paste-in [prompt](#tooltip-prompt), a saved [skill](#tooltip-skill), or a scheduled [agent](#tooltip-agent) that pulls straight from your dashboard export. Every version produces a draft for your review, never a final that ships on its own.

Open your AI chat and have it interview you into a scope document. Done means a written scope naming where your metrics and strategic notes live, the sections your update always needs, and what always gets flagged for your review before it goes out.

children.prompt: I want to build a system with my AI tool that turns our raw operating metrics and notes into a draft board or leadership update. Ask me questions, one at a time, about where our metrics and strategic notes actually live, what sections our updates always need, how much detail versus summary the audience wants, and what should always be flagged for my own review before it goes out. Then write it up as a scope document I can build from.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: the interview surfaces the sections and thresholds you'd otherwise skip, and the scope document becomes the brief for every reporting cycle after it.

items: Where the underlying metrics live (a dashboard, a spreadsheet, a data warehouse) and how current they are.
What tone and length this specific board or audience expects.
How much strategic [context](#tooltip-context) needs restating each cycle versus assuming continuity.

children.text: Bring the scope document. Pressure-test it first by pasting it into a fresh session or a different [model](#tooltip-model) and asking it to poke holes. Then gather any access it calls for. Common [tool connectors](#tooltip-tool-connectors) are your data and BI tools (a dashboard, Google Sheets, a data warehouse), your [knowledge base](#tooltip-personal-knowledge-base) ([Notion](#tooltip-notion), Google Docs) for strategic notes, and your slide or doc tool for the final format. The paste-in version needs none.
**Create.** Build your system and test it on this period's real numbers. The prompt below is an example. Your scope document gives a version for your setup.

children.prompt:
Goal: Draft this period's board update from our raw metrics and notes.

Context: Metrics: [paste data or link to dashboard export]. Strategic notes and major decisions this period: [paste]. Known risks: [paste]. Our update always covers: Performance, Strategic progress, Risks, Decisions made, What we need from the board.

Rules:
- State the number first, then the explanation. Never bury the headline.
- Where a metric moved, say why.
- Flag any number you're inferring rather than pulling directly from the data provided.
- Keep each section to 3 to 5 sentences.
- Output as a draft, clearly marked for my review, not a final.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: leading with the number keeps the update readable under time pressure, and flagging inferred numbers keeps you the one who verifies every figure before the board sees it.

children.text: **Review.** Check the draft against your scope. Headline first in every section, no unverified numbers, everything in the section it belongs in?
**Feedback.** Tell it exactly what's off ("summarize this section, don't [stack](#tooltip-stack) four decisions into one sentence") and fold each correction into the rules.

items: Build a "what changed since last update" [diff](#tooltip-diff) so you're not restating context every cycle.
Create audience-specific versions (board vs. all-hands) from the same draft.
Track which asks got board follow-through.

children.text: **Measure** with a [rubric](#tooltip-rubric). Have your AI chat turn the scope bar into pass/fail checks and a run log in one pass.

children.prompt: From my scope document, write a rubric for judging each board update, with 4 to 6 pass/fail checks. Then set up a simple run log I can keep in a doc or spreadsheet, with columns for date, period covered, sections revised, inferred numbers flagged, and board follow-through noted. Give me both in a format I can paste into my notes.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: pass/fail checks remove the judgment call, and the log columns make recurring drafting misses visible after a few reporting cycles.

children.text: **Log** every run against the rubric. Each entry takes a minute. Note the date, which rubric checks passed or failed, and what you changed. A single miss is noise, and a repeated miss is an instruction you haven't written yet.

**Make skills** from what the log shows. Once the system passes the rubric two cycles straight, package the prompt, section structure, and review rules into a reusable AI skill. [Claude](#tooltip-claude)'s built-in skill-creator skill will write it for you, and a custom GPT does the same in [ChatGPT](#tooltip-chatgpt).
One durable failure mode. Never let the draft state a number the underlying data doesn't support. You verify every figure before it goes to the board; the tool never sends anything unreviewed.
